title: Timer Schedule Drift After Manual Overrides
dataSources: Decoration timers (`holidaytimer:event`), birthday spending (`birthday:spend`), and fireworks noise events (`fireworks:noise`).
app: Seasonal household telemetry from decoration timers, birthday spending trackers, and fireworks noise sensors sent to Splunk HEC via Home Assistant, budget exports, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=holidaytimer:event
| search event_type="manual_override" schedule_drift_min=*
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(schedule_drift_min) as avg_schedule_drift_min max(schedule_drift_min) as max_schedule_drift_min by _time zone_name
| sort - _time
description: Tracks timer schedule drift after manual overrides over time and breaks it out by zone.
value: Override drift shows whether the automation still matches real life or keeps needing human correction.
implementation: Send timer schedule drift after manual overrides events to `index=personal` with the fields used in the breakdown and review the resulting trend at 1w granularity.
visualization: Stacked time chart of timer schedule drift after manual overrides by zone.
grandmaExplanation: It reveals how timer schedule drift after manual overrides changes over time so the busy spells and quiet spells stand out.
